headline: South Asia: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
- Asia: Suicide bombing at police checkpoint in Pakistan kills at least 11.
- Western Russia: Armiia TV channel suspends broadcasting due to Russian strikes.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns.
Unauthorized users accessed files containing the personal information of U.S. military personnel, a new breach notification letter warns.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: 8 sailors attempted suicide aboard ships from Lincoln strike group, Cao says.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed that eight sailors from the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Nellis Air Force Base says goodbye to last A-10 Thunderbolt II.
After five decades at the Nevada base, airmen saluted its last operational A-10 Warthog as it conducted its final flight Tuesday.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Bill blunder - Environmental levy bill withdrawn, replaced after certification cock-up.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Bill blunder - Environmental levy bill withdrawn, replaced after certification cock-up.
Debate on a bill titled ‘The Environmental Levy Act 2026’ had to be suspended on Friday in the Senate and the proposed statute withdrawn and replaced as the document that was first before the Upper House was not a money bill. This cock-up triggered a stern warning from acting leader of opposition business, Professor Floyd Morris, who described the error as unfortunate. Lengthy presentations were made on the bill and the senators had taken lunch break to resume deliberations.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: It’s been an intense hurricane season in the Pacific.
Tropical storms have spawned in the Pacific in what seems like assembly-line fashion in recent weeks, as El Niño conditions that emerged in June have caused waters to grow warmer than normal, setting off a chain of unusual weather around much of the world. “It’s ramping up to be perhaps the strongest El Niño on record,” University of Miami hurricane expert Brian McNoldy said.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Why AI has trouble predicting hurricane intensity.
THE CONVERSATION: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionised weather forecasting in just a few years, with global AI weather models now able to produce forecasts that rival some of the world’s best physics-based prediction systems. This remarkable progress has been driven by three factors: massive amounts of weather data, advances in AI models, and unprecedented computational power. While most of the current discussion on improving AI for weather focuses on the models or new hardware, the data is crucial.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: ‘He was too great to stop at his death’ - JP Samuels Youth Foundation keeps legacy alive.
For Alex Ward, losing his best friend Jean-Pierre ‘JP’ Samuels felt like losing a brother and a purpose at the same time. Samuels died on September 29, 2025 with so much still ahead of him. The 25-year-old had just finished his master’s degree in corporate finance and was about to start working at a wealth management firm so he could support his mother when he suddenly took ill and died shortly after. But instead of letting his name fade, Ward and a group of Samuels’ closest friends turned their grief into action and launched the JP Samuels Youth Foundation.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan police checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said. DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties. He clarified that no law enforcement or security personnel were among the deceased, which included a Customs official and civilians. The deceased comprised nine men, two women and a minor.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: What comes after Riyadh meeting between the Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish military chiefs?.
The hurried meeting of the military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Riyadh on Friday, followed by a separate meeting between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman points to how quickly the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is transitioning to an operational phase. The statements issued after the two meetings do not contain anything that would suggest that joint strikes or ground operations against Yemen’s Ansar Allah — commonly referred to as Houthis — are in the offing.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. “Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.

The attack occurred in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, said Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the provincial emergency service. The SkyStriker loitering munition executed a precision strike at Mahajan Field Firing Range during Yudh Abhyas 2026. This demonstration emphasized the importance of indigenous defence technology and unmanned systems in modern warfare. The military exercise aimed at enhancing interoperability between Indian and US forces was held recently. The SkyStriker can engage targets accurately using advanced target acquisition capabilities and operate quietly.

A complaint has been filed at Kotwali police station, accompanied by video evidence of the event, with law enforcement awaiting the next steps based on the allegations.
